## Motivation

Refs Ascend/sglang#1213.

The Kimi-K2.6 cookbook had no Ascend NPU option, although the Ascend NPU documentation ships verified Kimi-K2.6 best-practice recipes for both a single-node PD co-located shape and a two-node PD disaggregated shape. This PR adds both to the cookbook as a new "3.3 Ascend NPU Deployment" section, so users can obtain the correct command for each scenario without translating a platform-specific tutorial by hand.

## Modifications

- `docs/cookbook/autoregressive/Moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6.mdx` (+317 lines): a new **3.3 Ascend NPU Deployment** section with two scenario Tabs:
  - **1×A3 · PD Co-located (Low Latency)** — W4A8 + EAGLE3, TP16, reference TPOT ≈ 20 ms
  - **2×A3 · PD Disaggregated (High Throughput)** — prefill / decode / router commands split per node role, reference TPOT ≈ 100 ms
  - Per-scenario **measured accuracy and speed tables** (GSM8K, TPOT, TTFT, throughput, EAGLE3 acceptance)
  - Shared env block, launch commands, an inference-check curl, and a `bench_serving` command per scenario
  - A Warning documenting a device-OOM condition under burst load on self-built venvs (with the `--mem-fraction-static` mitigation), and a Note on the `ascend` transfer backend / `memfabric_hybrid` / driver-version setup
  - Cross-links to the Ascend tutorial, best-practices, and accuracy-evaluation pages
- Commands are transcribed from the verified best-practice recipes; deprecated flags are replaced with their current `main` spellings (`--cuda-graph-backend-{decode,prefill}=disabled`, `--cuda-graph-bs-decode`).

## Accuracy Tests

Verified on real Atlas 800I A3 hardware (16 dies/node, CANN 9.0.1, driver 26.1.1, SGLang Ascend fork @ fdebc93 with the ascend transfer-engine session-port fix).

| Scenario | Accuracy (EvalScope, GSM8K, limit 100) | Inference spot-checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1×A3 PD co-located | 98% | 5/5 correct |
| 2×A3 PD disaggregated | 99% | 5/5 correct |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`sglang.bench_serving`, random dataset, seed 1, via the router (port 6688).

**1×A3 PD co-located** (3.5k input / 1.5k output, max-concurrency 64, 256 prompts):

| Metric | Result | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Median time per output token | 21.5 ms | ≈ 20 ms |
| Mean time per output token | 26.55 ms | — |
| Output throughput | 1491 tok/s (peak 2745) | — |
| EAGLE3 acceptance length | 4.25 | — |

The median ITL is within ~7% of the 20 ms reference; the mean is pulled up by tail latency under a 64-way concurrent burst (P99 ITL 228 ms). Lowering `--mem-fraction-static` to 0.85 (from the 0.865 reference) was required on the self-built venv to avoid device OOM under that burst; the reference container image should run at the documented value.

**2×A3 PD disaggregated** (64k input / 1.5k output, max-concurrency 1, 1 prompt):

| Metric | Result | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Time per output token | 35.77 ms | ≈ 100 ms |
| Mean time to first token | 8318 ms (64k prefill) | — |

This is a single-request long-context latency run (the 100 ms reference is a TPOT target, not a throughput target), so no throughput row is reported.

## Documentation validation

- `mint validate` — build validation passed
- `mint dev` local preview — the Kimi-K2.6 page and the 3.3 section (both Tabs, all code blocks, all cross-links) render correctly; the page returns HTTP 200
- Flag spellings verified against current `main` (`server_args.py`): `--disable-cuda-graph` is a `DeprecatedStoreTrueAction`; the section uses the current `--cuda-graph-backend-{decode,prefill}=disabled` form instead
- Pre-commit / whitespace clean

## Checklist

- [x] Format code according to pre-commit
- [x] Update documentation and verify the local preview
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance

+</Note>

+

+### 3.3 Ascend NPU Deployment
+
+Kimi-K2.6 can also be deployed on the **Ascend A3 Series** (e.g., Atlas 800I A3) with the W4A8 INT8 quantized checkpoint and an EAGLE3 draft model for speculative decoding. Select **A3** as the hardware platform in the generator above, then pick a **Deployment Shape** to get the full command set:
+
+- **1×A3, PD co-located** — a single 8-card node serving prefill and decode together, tuned for low latency (reference TPOT ≈ 20 ms on 3.5k+1.5k).
+- **2×A3, PD disaggregated** — one prefill node plus one decode node behind the SGLang router, tuned for long-context throughput (reference TPOT ≈ 100 ms on 64k+1.5k).
+
+<Note>
+On the A3 Series each card has 2 dies and SGLang counts devices per die, so an 8-card node uses `--tp-size 16` (see [Ascend NPU Reference](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/reference/glossary#hardware)). For driver/CANN setup, the container image, and model weight download, follow the [Kimi-K2.6 Ascend Tutorial](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/tutorials/kimi_k2_6). +</Note>
+
+<Note>
+For the 2×A3 shape, cross-node KV transfer uses the `ascend` transfer backend (`memfabric`). Install `memfabric_hybrid` on both nodes (already in the reference container image), set `ASCEND_MF_STORE_URL` to the prefill node, and source the CANN environment in every shell that starts a server or the router. In minimal containers that mount only `driver/include` and `driver/lib64`, also make sure `/usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info` is present — see the [Ascend NPU installation guide](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/getting-started/installation) for driver and container setup.

detail.body:
## Motivation

Refs Ascend/sglang#1213.

The Kimi-K2.6 cookbook had no Ascend NPU option, although the Ascend NPU documentation ships verified Kimi-K2.6 best-practice recipes for both a single-node PD co-located shape and a two-node PD disaggregated shape. This PR adds both to the cookbook as a new "3.3 Ascend NPU Deployment" section, so users can obtain the correct command for each scenario without translating a platform-specific tutorial by hand.

## Modifications

- `docs/cookbook/autoregressive/Moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6.mdx` (+317 lines): a new **3.3 Ascend NPU Deployment** section with two scenario Tabs:
  - **1×A3 · PD Co-located (Low Latency)** — W4A8 + EAGLE3, TP16, reference TPOT ≈ 20 ms
  - **2×A3 · PD Disaggregated (High Throughput)** — prefill / decode / router commands split per node role, reference TPOT ≈ 100 ms
  - Per-scenario **measured accuracy and speed tables** (GSM8K, TPOT, TTFT, throughput, EAGLE3 acceptance)
  - Shared env block, launch commands, an inference-check curl, and a `bench_serving` command per scenario
  - A Warning documenting a device-OOM condition under burst load on self-built venvs (with the `--mem-fraction-static` mitigation), and a Note on the `ascend` transfer backend / `memfabric_hybrid` / driver-version setup
  - Cross-links to the Ascend tutorial, best-practices, and accuracy-evaluation pages
- Commands are transcribed from the verified best-practice recipes; deprecated flags are replaced with their current `main` spellings (`--cuda-graph-backend-{decode,prefill}=disabled`, `--cuda-graph-bs-decode`).

## Accuracy Tests

Verified on real Atlas 800I A3 hardware (16 dies/node, CANN 9.0.1, driver 26.1.1, SGLang Ascend fork @ fdebc93 with the ascend transfer-engine session-port fix).

| Scenario | Accuracy (EvalScope, GSM8K, limit 100) | Inference spot-checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1×A3 PD co-located | 98% | 5/5 correct |
| 2×A3 PD disaggregated | 99% | 5/5 correct |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`sglang.bench_serving`, random dataset, seed 1, via the router (port 6688).

**1×A3 PD co-located** (3.5k input / 1.5k output, max-concurrency 64, 256 prompts):

| Metric | Result | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Median time per output token | 21.5 ms | ≈ 20 ms |
| Mean time per output token | 26.55 ms | — |

+### 3.3 Ascend NPU Deployment
+
+Kimi-K2.6 can also be deployed on the **Ascend A3 Series** (e.g., Atlas 800I A3) with the W4A8 INT8 quantized checkpoint and an EAGLE3 draft model for speculative decoding. Select **A3** as the hardware platform in the generator above, then pick a **Deployment Shape** to get the full command set:
+
+- **1×A3, PD co-located** — a single 8-card node serving prefill and decode together, tuned for low latency (reference TPOT ≈ 20 ms on 3.5k+1.5k).
+- **2×A3, PD disaggregated** — one prefill node plus one decode node behind the SGLang router, tuned for long-context throughput (reference TPOT ≈ 100 ms on 64k+1.5k).
+
+<Note>
+On the A3 Series each card has 2 dies and SGLang counts devices per die, so an 8-card node uses `--tp-size 16` (see [Ascend NPU Reference](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/reference/glossary#hardware)). For driver/CANN setup, the container image, and model weight download, follow the [Kimi-K2.6 Ascend Tutorial](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/tutorials/kimi_k2_6). The full tuning matrix (including 2-node PD-mixed and prefix-cache variants) lives in [Kimi-K2.6 Ascend Best Practices](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/best-practices/kimi_k2_6).
+</Note>
+
+<Note>
+For the 2×A3 shape, cross-node KV transfer uses the `ascend` transfer backend (`memfabric`). Install `memfabric_hybrid` on both nodes (already in the reference container image), set `ASCEND_MF_STORE_URL` to the prefill node, and source the CANN environment in every shell that starts a server or the router. In minimal containers that mount only `driver/include` and `driver/lib64`, also make sure `/usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info` is present — see the [Ascend NPU installation guide](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/getting-started/installation) for driver and container setup.
+</Note>
+
+Startup takes several minutes (126 weight shards plus CUDA-graph capture); the server is ready when the log prints `The server is fired up and ready to roll!`. Verify with a chat request — the co-located server listens on port `30000`; for the PD shape send requests to the router on port `6688`:
+
+```bash Command
+curl http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \
+  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+  -d "{
+    \"model\": \"$MODEL_PATH\",
+    \"messages\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"What is 17 + 25?\"}],
+    \"max_tokens\": 256
+  }"
+```
+
+Benchmark the co-located shape (random dataset, 3.5k input / 1.5k output, concurrency 64):
+
+```bash Command
+python -m sglang.bench_serving \
+    --dataset-name random \
+    --backend sglang \
+    --host 127.0.0.1 \
+    --port 30000 \
+    --max-concurrency 64 \
+    --num-prompts 256 \
+    --random-input-len 3500 \
+    --random-output-len 1500 \
+    --random-range-ratio 1 \
+    --warmup-requests 0 \
+    --seed 1
+```
+
+Measured on one Atlas 800I A3 server (16 dies, W4A8 + EAGLE3, `--mem-fraction-static 0.85`):
